subproblem.title: Agreement on C_c(O) implies agreement on bounded Borel functions vanishing off O (π–λ)
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ on ℝ^P, all g₁, g₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with g₁ μ₁-integrable and g₂ μ₂-integrable, and every open O ⊆ ℝ^P: if ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every continuous φ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O, then ∫ h g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ h g₂ dμ₂ for every Borel measurable h : ℝ^P → ℝ that is bounded (|h(x)| ≤ C for some constant C and all x) and vanishes outside O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g₁ g₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g₁ μ₁ → Integrable g₂ μ₂ → ∀ O : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen O → (∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ O → ∫ x, φ x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, φ x * g₂ x ∂μ₂) → ∀ h : Eucl P → ℝ, Measurable h → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, |h x| ≤ C) → (∀ x, x ∉ O → h x = 0) → ∫ x, h x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, h x * g₂ x ∂μ₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof: finite measures λ₁ and λ₂, equality on open subsets by monotone convergence, the π–λ theorem, then bounded Borel integrands. Here O is any open set and g₁, g₂ are any integrable functions; the parent uses O = W′ and g_i = g_i^β.

Setting. μ₁, μ₂ are Borel measures on ℝ^P; g_i is μ_i-integrable (i = 1, 2); O ⊆ ℝ^P is open. Hypothesis (H): ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel with |h| ≤ C and h = 0 outside O.

0. (Borel representatives.) Each g_i is μ_i-integrable, hence μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable; choose a Borel g̃_i with g̃_i = g_i μ_i-a.e. Then g̃_i is μ_i-integrable, and ∫ f g_i dμ_i = ∫ f g̃_i dμ_i for every function f, because the integrands agree μ_i-a.e. Hypothesis (H) and the conclusion involve only integrals of this form, so it suffices to prove the claim for g̃₁, g̃₂. From now on, assume g₁ and g₂ are Borel.

1. (Two finite measures.) For t ∈ ℝ let t⁺ := max(t, 0) and t⁻ := max(−t, 0), so t = t⁺ − t⁻ and 0 ≤ t^± ≤ |t|. Define Borel measures
 λ₁(B) := ∫_B g₁⁺ dμ₁ + ∫_B g₂⁻ dμ₂ and λ₂(B) := ∫_B g₁⁻ dμ₁ + ∫_B g₂⁺ dμ₂.
 These are sums of measures with nonnegative Borel densities (μ_i.withDensity of ENNReal.ofReal of ±g_i). Both are finite, since λ_i(ℝ^P) ≤ ∫|g₁| dμ₁ + ∫|g₂| dμ₂ < ∞.

2. (Integration identity.) Let f be Borel with |f| ≤ D. Then f is λ₁- and λ₂-integrable, being bounded and measurable on finite measures. Integrating against a sum of measures and against measures with densities gives
 ∫ f dλ₁ = ∫ f g₁⁺ dμ₁ + ∫ f g₂⁻ dμ₂ and ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁⁻ dμ₁ + ∫ f g₂⁺ dμ₂.
 All four integrals on the right are finite because |f g_i^±| ≤ D|g_i|. Subtracting and using g_i⁺ − g_i⁻ = g_i gives
 (★) ∫ f dλ₁ − ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ f g₂ dμ₂.
 In particular, by (H), ∫ φ dλ₁ = ∫ φ dλ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O, since such φ are bounded and Borel.

3. (Equality on open subsets of O.) Let V ⊆ O be open; we show λ₁(V) = λ₂(V). For j ≥ 1 let b_j(x) := max(0, min(1, j − |x|)). If V ≠ ℝ^P let a_j(x) := min(1, max(0, j·infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) − 1)); if V = ℝ^P let a_j :≡ 1. Put φ_j := a_j·b_j.
 (i) φ_j is continuous (x ↦ infDist(x, S) is 1-Lipschitz and |·| is continuous), and 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1.
 (ii) If φ_j(x) ≠ 0, then |x| < j and, when V ≠ ℝ^P, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) > 1/j. So φ_j = 0 outside F_j := B̄(0, j) ∩ {x : infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/j} (F_j := B̄(0, j) if V = ℝ^P). F_j is closed and bounded, hence compact. Moreover F_j ⊆ V, because every point of ℝ^P ∖ V has infDist 0 < 1/j to ℝ^P ∖ V. Hence φ_j has compact support and tsupport φ_j ⊆ F_j ⊆ V ⊆ O.
 (iii) φ_j(x) increases to 1_V(x) for every x. Indeed a_j(x) and b_j(x) are nonnegative and nondecreasing in j. If x ∈ V and V ≠ ℝ^P, then d := infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) > 0, because ℝ^P ∖ V is closed, nonempty and does not contain x; so a_j(x) = 1 once j ≥ 2/d. If V = ℝ^P, a_j(x) = 1. In both cases b_j(x) = 1 once j ≥ |x| + 1. If x ∉ V, then infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, so a_j(x) = 0 and φ_j(x) = 0.
 By step 2, ∫ φ_j dλ₁ = ∫ φ_j dλ₂ for every j. Since 0 ≤ φ_j ↑ 1_V and λ_i is finite, the monotone convergence theorem (or dominated convergence with dominating function 1) gives ∫ φ_j dλ_i → λ_i(V) for i = 1, 2. Hence λ₁(V) = λ₂(V).

4. (Equality on all Borel subsets of O: π–λ.) Let ν_i(B) := λ_i(B ∩ O), the restriction of λ_i to the Borel set O; ν₁ and ν₂ are finite Borel measures. For every open G ⊆ ℝ^P, G ∩ O is an open subset of O, so ν₁(G) = λ₁(G ∩ O) = λ₂(G ∩ O) = ν₂(G) by step 3; in particular ν₁(ℝ^P) = ν₂(ℝ^P). The open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P. By the π–λ uniqueness theorem for finite measures (Mathlib ext_of_generate_finite with isPiSystem_isOpen), ν₁ = ν₂.

5. (Conclusion.) h is bounded, Borel and vanishes outside O, so ∫ h dλ_i = ∫_O h dλ_i = ∫ h dν_i for i = 1, 2. Step 4 then gives ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂. Applying (★) with f = h gives ∫ h g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ h g₂ dμ₂. ∎

Formalization note (optional): in Lean, steps 3–4 can be replaced by Radon–Nikodym densities f_i := dλ_i/d(λ₁ + λ₂) together with Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero. Smooth compactly supported functions are continuous, so step 2 gives ∫ ψ·(f₁ − f₂) d(λ₁ + λ₂) = 0 for every such ψ with tsupport ψ ⊆ O. Hence f₁ = f₂ (λ₁ + λ₂)-a.e. on O, and ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ f₁ h d(λ₁ + λ₂) = ∫ f₂ h d(λ₁ + λ₂) = ∫ h dλ₂.
proof_key_steps: Replace g_i by Borel μ_i-a.e. representatives; no integral changes.
Form the finite Borel measures λ₁ = g₁⁺μ₁ + g₂⁻μ₂ and λ₂ = g₁⁻μ₁ + g₂⁺μ₂.
Identity (★): ∫ f dλ₁ − ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ f g₂ dμ₂ for bounded Borel f; hence λ₁ and λ₂ agree on C_c(O).
Continuous cutoffs φ_j ↑ 1_V with tsupport φ_j ⊆ V give λ₁(V) = λ₂(V) for every open V ⊆ O (monotone convergence).
π–λ: the finite measures λ₁⌞O and λ₂⌞O agree on the open sets, hence are equal.
For bounded Borel h vanishing off O, ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂; conclude with (★).

audit.reason: The prose and one-line type agree, including integrability, Borel measurability, global boundedness and vanishing outside O. Borel representatives legitimately preserve the integrals. Positive and negative densities define finite measures, and the integration identity has integrable terms. The explicit cutoffs have compact support inside V and increase to its indicator, including the full-space case. Finite-measure π–λ uniqueness gives equality of restrictions, which proves the bounded-integrand conclusion. No circular dependence or missing regularity assumption remains.

subproblem.title: Coordinate expansion of k-covectors on ℝ^P (Fact A)
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ and every k-covector α on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ, Covector (Eucl P) k): α = Σ_{β ∈ I(k,P)} α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(k−1)})·dx^β. Here I(k,P) = SimonMultiIndex k P is the finite set of strictly increasing maps (order embeddings) β : Fin k → Fin P; e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the i-th standard basis vector, so the coefficient is euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β; and dx^β = wedgeCovectors k (j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)) is the wedge of the coordinate 1-covectors dx^{β(0)}, …, dx^{β(k−1)}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) k), α = ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex k P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β • wedgeCovectors k (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Fact A of the parent proof (every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β), used in its step 7.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P) is the standard basis of ℝ^P, and dx^i := EuclideanSpace.proj i, so dx^i(y) = y_i and dx^i(e_l) = δ_{il}. For ι : Fin k → Fin P write e_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(k−1)}). For β ∈ I(k,P) = SimonMultiIndex k P (strictly increasing β : Fin k → Fin P), α(e_β) = euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors k (j ↦ dx^{β(j)}). Let α be a k-covector and α' := Σ_{β ∈ I(k,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β. We show α = α'.

1. (Values of dx^β on basis tuples.) Let β, γ ∈ I(k,P). By SimonGMT's wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} := dx^{β(i)}(e_{γ(j)}) for i, j ∈ Fin k. This entry is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.

2. (Kronecker property dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.) If γ = β, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective), so M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1. Now let γ ≠ β. The ranges R_β := β(Fin k) and R_γ := γ(Fin k) both have exactly k elements. If R_γ ⊆ R_β, equal cardinalities force R_γ = R_β. But two strictly increasing maps Fin k → Fin P with the same range are equal, since each is the increasing enumeration of its range (Mathlib StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT); this contradicts γ ≠ β. So some j₀ has γ(j₀) ∉ R_β. Then column j₀ of M is zero, and det M = 0.

3. (Agreement on increasing basis tuples.) For γ ∈ I(k,P), step 2 gives α'(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β(e_γ) = α(e_γ).

4. (Agreement on injective basis tuples.) Let ι : Fin k → Fin P be injective. Choose a permutation σ of Fin k such that ι∘σ is monotone, by sorting (Mathlib Tuple.sort and Tuple.monotone_sort). Since ι∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := ι∘σ ∈ I(k,P) and e_ι = e_γ∘σ⁻¹. Every alternating map f and permutation τ satisfy f(v∘τ) = sign(τ)·f(v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Hence, using step 3, α(e_ι) = sign(σ⁻¹)·α(e_γ) = sign(σ⁻¹)·α'(e_γ) = α'(e_ι).

5. (Conclusion.) An alternating k-linear map f on ℝ^P is determined by its values on the tuples e_ι with ι injective. Indeed, expanding each argument in the basis, multilinearity gives f(v_0, …, v_{k−1}) = Σ_{ι : Fin k → Fin P} (Π_j (v_j)_{ι(j)})·f(e_ι), and the terms with non-injective ι vanish because f is alternating (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext_alternating, for the basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose i-th vector is e_i). By step 4 the alternating maps underlying α and α' agree on all such tuples, so they are equal. A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Hence α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
The argument is uniform in k and P. For k = 0, I(0,P) has exactly one element, the empty tuple is injective and increasing, and the 0×0 determinant is 1. For k > P, I(k,P) = ∅ and the right side is 0; there is no injective ι : Fin k → Fin P, so step 5 gives α = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^β(e_γ) = det[δ_{β(i)γ(j)}]_{i,j} by wedgeCovectors_apply_det.
Kronecker property dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}: the matrix is the identity if β = γ, and has a zero column otherwise (strictly increasing maps with equal range coincide).
α and α' := Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β agree on increasing basis tuples.
Sorting plus the sign rule for alternating maps extends the agreement to all injective basis tuples.
Basis extensionality for alternating maps (Module.Basis.ext_alternating) gives α = α'.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the stated coordinate expansion and the pinned definitions of coefficients and wedges. Determinant evaluation establishes the Kronecker property; equal finite ranges force equal increasing indices, justifying the zero-column argument. Sorting and the alternating sign rule extend equality to injective basis tuples, and basis extensionality completes the proof. The k=0 and k>P cases are covered. The proof is independent of the selected parent and other active branches.

subproblem.title: Test-form integrability gives integrability of x ↦ v(x)(c) on compact subsets of U
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ and every open U ⊆ ℝ^P: let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P and v : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) k, i.e. each v(x) is a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) be such that x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable for every test form ω ∈ D^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: smooth of every finite order, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then for every compact L ⊆ U and every k-covector c ∈ Λ^k(ℝ^P) (Covector (Eucl P) k), the function x ↦ v(x)(c) is μ-integrable on L.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, Integrable (fun x => v x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x)) μ) → ∀ L : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact L → L ⊆ U → ∀ c : Covector (Eucl P) k, IntegrableOn (fun x => v x c) L μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (testing with χ·dx^β where χ = 1 near a compact set). Here it is stated for an arbitrary compact L ⊆ U and an arbitrary constant covector c; the parent uses L = K_r and c = dx^β.

Setting. P, k ∈ ℕ; U ⊆ ℝ^P is open; μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^P; v : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P), where each v(x) is a continuous linear functional on k-covectors. Assume x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable for every ω ∈ D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (ω smooth of every finite order, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U). Fix a compact L ⊆ U and a k-covector c. If L = ∅ there is nothing to prove, so assume L ≠ ∅.

1. (Room around L.) L is compact, U is open and L ⊆ U, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ L = {x : infDist(x, L) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).

2. (Smooth cutoff: a mollified indicator.) Put ε := δ/3 and E := cthickening ε L. Let ρ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with ρ ≥ 0, ρ = 0 outside the closed ball B̄(0, ε), and ∫ ρ dℒ^P = 1 (a normalized bump function). Define χ(x) := ∫ ρ(x − y)·1_E(y) dℒ^P(y).
 (a) χ is C^∞. It is the convolution of the compactly supported C^∞ function ρ with the bounded Borel function 1_E, which vanishes outside the bounded set E. Differentiating under the integral sign puts every derivative on ρ.
 (b) 0 ≤ χ ≤ ∫ ρ = 1.
 (c) χ = 1 on L. If x ∈ L and ρ(x − y) ≠ 0, then |y − x| ≤ ε, so infDist(y, L) ≤ |y − x| ≤ ε and y ∈ E. Hence χ(x) = ∫ ρ(x − y) dℒ^P(y) = 1.
 (d) Compact support inside U. If χ(x) ≠ 0, there is y ∈ E with ρ(x − y) ≠ 0, so infDist(x, L) ≤ |x − y| + infDist(y, L) ≤ 2ε. Hence χ = 0 outside the closed set cthickening (2ε) L, so tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening (2ε) L ⊆ cthickening δ L ⊆ U. This set is closed and bounded (L is bounded), hence compact, so χ has compact support.
 Alternatively, the smooth Urysohn lemma gives a χ with the properties used below (C^∞, χ = 1 on L, χ = 0 outside cthickening δ L): apply Mathlib exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) and n = ⊤ : ℕ∞ to the closed set L ⊆ interior(cthickening δ L). Then tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening δ L, which is compact and contained in U.

3. (A test form.) Define ω(x) := χ(x)·c. ω is C^∞, being a C^∞ scalar function times a constant covector. Also support ω ⊆ support χ, so tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport χ, which is compact and contained in U. Hence ω ∈ D^k(U).

4. (Integrability of χ·v(·)(c).) By hypothesis x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable. By linearity of v(x), v(x)(ω(x)) = v(x)(χ(x)·c) = χ(x)·v(x)(c). So x ↦ χ(x)v(x)(c) is μ-integrable on ℝ^P, and in particular on L.

5. (Conclusion.) L is compact, hence closed, hence Borel. By 2(c), χ(x)v(x)(c) = v(x)(c) for every x ∈ L. A function that agrees on the measurable set L with a function integrable on L is itself integrable on L. Therefore x ↦ v(x)(c) is μ-integrable on L. ∎

Formalization note: the frozen Lean statement binds a variable named ω, so it must not be elaborated under `open scoped ContDiff`, where ω is notation for analytic smoothness.
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ L ⊆ U (compact set inside an open set).
Build a C^∞ cutoff χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on L, and tsupport χ compact ⊆ cthickening δ L ⊆ U (mollified indicator of cthickening (δ/3) L, or the smooth Urysohn lemma).
The form ω := χ·c is a test form in D^k(U).
The hypothesis and linearity of v(x) make x ↦ χ(x)·v(x)(c) μ-integrable.
Since χ = 1 on the Borel set L, x ↦ v(x)(c) is μ-integrable on L.

Linearity and the assumed test-form integrability yield an integrable function agreeing with v(·)(c) on measurable L. The empty case is covered. No measurability or local-finiteness assumption on the original data is silently added, and no parent or sibling theorem is used.

subproblem.title: Agreement of g₁μ₁ and g₂μ₂ on C_c^∞(O) extends to C_c(O)
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ on ℝ^P, all g₁, g₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with g₁ μ₁-integrable and g₂ μ₂-integrable, and every open O ⊆ ℝ^P: if ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → ℝ (smooth of every finite order; Lean ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O, then ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every continuous φ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g₁ g₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g₁ μ₁ → Integrable g₂ μ₂ → ∀ O : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen O → (∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ O → ∫ x, φ x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, φ x * g₂ x ∂μ₂) → ∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ O → ∫ x, φ x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, φ x * g₂ x ∂μ₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (agreement on continuous functions via mollification and dominated convergence). Here O is any open set and g₁, g₂ are any integrable functions; the parent uses O = W′ and g_i = g_i^β = 1_{K_r}·v_i(dx^β).

Setting. μ₁, μ₂ are Borel measures on ℝ^P; g_i is μ_i-integrable (i = 1, 2); O ⊆ ℝ^P is open. Hypothesis (H): ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every φ that is C^∞ (smooth of every finite order) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O. Fix a continuous φ with compact support and K := tsupport φ ⊆ O. If K = ∅, then φ ≡ 0 and both sides vanish, so assume K ≠ ∅.

1. (Preliminaries.) K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is s > 0 with cthickening s K ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Since φ is continuous with compact support, there is M ≥ 0 with |φ(x)| ≤ M for all x.

2. (Mollification.) For j ∈ ℕ let ε_j := s/(j + 2), so 0 < ε_j < s and ε_j → 0. Let ρ_j be C^∞ with ρ_j ≥ 0, ρ_j = 0 outside B̄(0, ε_j) and ∫ ρ_j dℒ^P = 1. Set φ_j(x) := ∫ ρ_j(x − y) φ(y) dℒ^P(y).
 (a) φ_j is C^∞: it is the convolution of a compactly supported C^∞ function with a continuous compactly supported function, and one may differentiate under the integral sign.
 (b) If φ_j(x) ≠ 0, some y has ρ_j(x − y) ≠ 0 and φ(y) ≠ 0, so |x − y| ≤ ε_j and y ∈ K; hence infDist(x, K) ≤ ε_j. So φ_j = 0 outside cthickening ε_j K, which is closed and bounded, hence compact. Therefore φ_j has compact support and tsupport φ_j ⊆ cthickening ε_j K ⊆ cthickening s K ⊆ O.
 (c) |φ_j(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_j(x − y)|φ(y)| dy ≤ M·∫ ρ_j = M for all x.
 (d) For each x, |φ_j(x) − φ(x)| = |∫ ρ_j(x − y)(φ(y) − φ(x)) dy| ≤ sup{|φ(y) − φ(x)| : |y − x| ≤ ε_j}. This tends to 0 as j → ∞ by continuity of φ at x, so φ_j(x) → φ(x).

3. (Smooth agreement.) By (a), (b) and (H), ∫ φ_j g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ_j g₂ dμ₂ for every j.

4. (Dominated convergence.) Fix i ∈ {1, 2}. Each φ_j g_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable, since φ_j is continuous and g_i is integrable. By (c), |φ_j g_i| ≤ M|g_i|, and M|g_i| is μ_i-integrable. By (d), φ_j g_i → φ g_i pointwise. The dominated convergence theorem gives ∫ φ_j g_i dμ_i → ∫ φ g_i dμ_i.

5. (Conclusion.) By step 3 the sequences in step 4 for i = 1 and i = 2 coincide term by term, so their limits are equal: ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂. ∎

Formalization note: instead of convolution, the approximants may be taken from Mathlib's Continuous.exists_contDiff_approx (module Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.SmoothApprox), with n = ⊤ and constant tolerance 1/(j + 1). It gives C^∞ functions ψ_j with |ψ_j − φ| < 1/(j + 1) and support ψ_j ⊆ support φ. Then tsupport ψ_j ⊆ K ⊆ O, ψ_j has compact support, |ψ_j| ≤ M + 1 and ψ_j → φ pointwise, so steps 3–5 apply verbatim with dominating functions (M + 1)|g_i|.
proof_key_steps: K := tsupport φ is a compact subset of O; choose s > 0 with cthickening s K ⊆ O and a bound |φ| ≤ M.
Mollify: φ_j := ρ_{ε_j} * φ with ε_j = s/(j+2) is C^∞, compactly supported with tsupport ⊆ cthickening ε_j K ⊆ O, satisfies |φ_j| ≤ M, and φ_j → φ pointwise.
Apply the smooth hypothesis to each φ_j: ∫ φ_j g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ_j g₂ dμ₂.
Dominated convergence with dominating functions M|g_i| gives ∫ φ_j g_i dμ_i → ∫ φ g_i dμ_i.
Termwise-equal convergent sequences have equal limits.
